records.subject: Aviation safety incident at CSMI Airport Mumbai
records.SM_Text:
Shri Milind Murli Deora: On June 8th an IndiGo aircraft touched down at Mumbai?s Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport merely seconds after an Air India aircraft took off. At the time, the distance between the two aircrafts was barely 2,000 feet. This was one of the closest - and scariest - air traffic incidents in recent history. In response to my letter, the DGCA assured an investigation and corrective action for the incident. Mumbai?s airport is one of the world?s busiest single-runway airports, handling nearly 1000 flights daily, with up to 46 arrivals and departures per hour. Last year, the airport handled almost 4.4 crore passengers with flight operations rising from 1,86,000 in FY22 to 2,90,000 in FY23. Despite the Civil Aviation Ministry?s 14 February 2024 directive to reduce flight numbers, the summer schedule saw an 8% increase in weekly flight movement, clearly indicating the need for a permanent solution to decongest CSMIA. The only long-term solution is the timely completion of the Navi Mumbai International Airport in Ulwe. I urge the Government at both the Centre and in Maharashtra for accelerating its development and targeting commercial operations by 31st March 2025 and ensuring that every effort be made to prevent any further delays in its operationalization. Additionally, I urge the Civil Aviation Ministry to invest in developing indigenous AI technology to assist ATC towers in managing traffic more efficiently. Embracing innovative technology will not only enhance safety but also position us as leaders in aviation management.

(Ends)

records.subject: BHARAT SMALL REACTORS FOR INDUSTRIAL DECARBONISATION
records.extent:
(a) A Request For Proposal (RFP) for setting up 220MW Bharat Small Reactors (BSRs) was 
published by NPCIL. In response, NPCIL has received a proposal from one private 
industry i.e. M/s Hindalco Industries Ltd. Further discussions are in between the two sides 
to finalise the project details. 
The 
possibility of reduction in land usage up to about 90 hectare, subject to radiological impact 
assessment is being evaluated.

records.subject: SAFETY OF AIR OPERATIONS AND DGCA OVERSIGHT
records.extent:
With regard to the AI 171 crash that happened
in June last year, the investigation is going at a very good pace and all the resources that are
required for AIB, which is the primary agency looking into the investigation, the Ministry is
providing that and I would say that very soon, before the completion of this year, the report
should be out.

records.subject: GREEN TUG TRANSITION PROGRAMME
records.extent:
(a) & (b) Yes, four Major Ports, viz. Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority, Deendayal Port Authority,
V.O. Chidambaranar Port Authority and Paradip Port Authority have been selected in Phase 1 of
the Green Tug Transition Programme (GTTP) with the target of procuring / hiring at least two
green tugs by each port.
